quote: The door itself / makes no promises. / It is only a door.
source: Adrienne Rich, Prospective Immigrants Please Note, closing lines, Snapshots of a Daughter-in-Law (Harper and Row, 1963)
note: Corrected publisher. Snapshots of a Daughter-in-Law, Poems 1954 to 1962, was first published by Harper and Row in 1963; W. W. Norton reissued the book in 1967, so the proposal put Norton on the first edition. The wording and the three line close are confirmed.

evidence.where: Full texts of the poem read at two sites, which agree that the poem is written in tercets throughout, opening Either you will / go through this door / or you will not go through., and closing The door itself / makes no promises. / It is only a door. as three separate lines. Bookseller listings of the 1963 first edition name Harper and Row as the publisher, and separate listings show W. W. Norton issuing the book in 1967.
evidence.edition: Adrienne Rich, Snapshots of a Daughter-in-Law: Poems 1954 to 1962 (Harper and Row, 1963)
evidence.locator: Prospective Immigrants Please Note, the closing three lines

reason: The three lines close the poem in the wording and lineation proposed and end in a full stop; only the imprint was wrong. Rich is unbanned and stands at nought for the year, and the line is not shipped anywhere in First Light. Plain speech about a choice that is genuinely open, offering no counsel and needing no warning.
